This definition ranges over $\mathbb N$-indexed covers with strictly positive weights, and finite-frame costs are compared through padding and a limit in `PositiveWeightPadding.lean`.

short.e.divisor-set.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.d: The finite set $\{qd:d\mid\prod_{p\in P}p\}$. The definition forms the divisors of the product and multiplies each by $q$. No primality or positivity hypotheses are needed merely to define this `Finset`. The subsequent expansion theorems assume $q>0$ and prime elements of $P$. For $q=2$ and $P=\{3,5\}$ it gives $\{2,6,10,30\}$. Its divisor count records which of these selected exponents divide the observation index.

short.e.prime-mass.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.p: The finite sum $S=\sum_{p\in P}1/p$. Lean calls it `primeReciprocalMass P`, with each summand interpreted as a real number. The definition accepts a finite set of natural numbers. The hypotheses `hP : ∀ p ∈ P, Nat.Prime p` in subsequent theorems make these selected numbers primes. This parameter controls both the mean number of available prime divisors and the optimized cover cost. The upper bound $eS/q$ later requires $S\ge1$.

short.e.optimal-two-sided.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.o: Lean gives these bounds for its infimum over countably indexed strictly positive-weight covers, whereas the paper directly includes finite covers. `PositiveWeightPadding` compares a single finite frame with that infimum, and a general equality of the two cover-class infima is not asserted here. Lean also permits $q>0$ and common prime factors between $q$ and $P$.

short.e.rank-mean.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.c: The prose states the mean $\mathbb E[Z\mid q\mid n]=S$. Lean states the unconditional finite mean of the $qp$-divisibility count as $S/q$. Dividing by the frequency $1/q$ identifies the conditional mean.

short.e.scalar-linear-bound.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.e: For every real $z$, the scalar cost at $2^z$ is at least $e(z-1)$. Lean proves this inequality for every real $z$, whereas the paragraph works with $z\ge0$.

short.e.product-upper-bound.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.c: Lean bounds $q^{-1}\prod_{p\in P}(1+z/p)$ by $\exp(zS)/q$. The display divides by $z$ and specializes to $z=1/S$. It also calls this a cover cost, which uses the separate cube-majorant construction.

short.sources.weighted-theorem.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.d: The first conjunct is the fixed-base irrationality assertion. The source definition spells out its hypotheses. An infinite support with finite weighted sum at an integer base $b\ge2$ has irrational $X_A(b)$.

short.sources.weighted-heredity.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.f: `finitePrimeWeighted_fixedBase_hereditary` puts the weighted hypothesis on the positive host `H`. At the fixed base $b\ge2$, every infinite set `A` contained in that host inherits irrationality of its subseries.

short.sources.mixed-theorem.ErdosProblems.Erdos257.PaperCompleteR8.a: `arbitraryWeightMixedSupport_allBase_hereditary` is the proof with positive cover data supplied as `LogBudgetCover V`.
